title: Bike gears skipping: chain, cassette and barrel adjuster
description: User wanted brief help with gears skipping on small rear cogs; chain 0.75% worn, Dorothy advised new chain, likely cassette, and barrel adjuster steps.
abstract: The user's bike skips under load on the smallest rear cogs, and they asked for brief answers. Dorothy gave a prioritized checklist: barrel adjuster and cable tension, chain wear, shark-fin cog wear, derailleur hanger alignment, and cable condition. The chain measured 0.75% worn, so she advised replacing the chain and probably the cassette, since the small cogs have likely worn to match the chain. She suggested checking for hooked cog and chainring teeth, and a mid-range cassette to save money. The user then asked how to adjust the barrel adjuster after fitting the new chain. Dorothy gave short steps: shift up one cog; counterclockwise adds tension if it hesitates; clockwise reduces it if it overshoots; use half-turns; limit screws if the chain can't reach the end cogs; recheck after the first ride. Left open: drivetrain type, chain mileage, cog condition, whether they replaced the cassette, and whether the fix worked. The user prefers short answers, as in the sourdough chat.
